It carries a hungry Dalit’s message to Lord Shiva.

Transfer of all temple conservation functions to the Archaeological Survey of India

s: Which museum is chiefly associated with the Mahachaitya and the white limestone sculpture of the Amaravati School?
x: The Amaravati site museum is associated with the Amaravati Mahachaitya and the white limestone sculptures of the Amaravati School.

o: Victoria Jubilee Museum – Salar Jung Museum

s: What was the former name of the Bapu Museum, Vijayawada?
x: The Bapu Museum in Vijayawada was formerly the Victoria Jubilee Museum.

s: In which museum is the 'Veiled Rebecca' (Rome, 1876) displayed?

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched (museum – place)?

x: The AP State Museum at Hyderabad is now the Telangana State Museum.

s: Who founded the Archaeological Survey of India in 1861?
x: Alexander Cunningham founded the ASI in 1861; Ranganatha Saraswati found Nagarjunakonda (1926) and Longhurst dug it (1927).

s: In which year was Lepakshi placed on UNESCO's tentative list of World Heritage Sites?
x: Lepakshi, including the Veerabhadra temple and monolithic Nandi, was placed on the tentative list in 2022; Andhra Pradesh has no inscribed World Heritage Site.

s: How many inscribed UNESCO World Heritage Sites does Andhra Pradesh have?
x: AP has no inscribed World Heritage Site; Lepakshi is only on the tentative list.

s: Where is the 153-ft gopuram under ASI conservation in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The 153-ft gopuram of Mangalagiri is under ASI conservation; Lepakshi is known for its monolithic Nandi.

s: Lepakshi, on UNESCO's tentative list, is famous for its Veerabhadra temple and for which of the following?
x: Lepakshi has the Veerabhadra temple and a monolithic Nandi; the 153-ft gopuram is at Mangalagiri.

s: In which village of the Amaravati capital region are the interim Andhra Pradesh Secretariat and Legislature buildings located?
x: The interim Government Complex with the Secretariat and the Legislature is at Velagapudi, Thullur mandal, in the Amaravati capital region.

s: In which year was the Andhra Pradesh Legislature building at Velagapudi inaugurated?
x: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu inaugurated the Legislature building at Velagapudi on 2 March 2017.

s: Nagarjunakonda was first found in 1926 by whom?
x: Nagarjunakonda was found in 1926 by A. Ranganatha Saraswati. Later excavation work involved Longhurst, Ramachandran and R. Subrahmanyam.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Nagarjunakonda?
o: It has an acoustic building and an amphitheatre.
It shows habitation from the Palaeolithic to 1960 CE.
It has Santamula's Ashvamedha altar and a Sati sculpture.

x: Nagarjunakonda has more than 30 stupas, so 'fewer than ten' is false; the other three features are all associated with the site.

s: Submergence by which dam led to the rebuilding of monuments at Anupu and on Nagarjunakonda island on higher ground?
x: The area was submerged after 1960 by the Nagarjunasagar Dam, so the ASI dismantled and rebuilt the monuments ('transplantation of monuments').

x: Longhurst dug Nagarjunakonda in 1927; A. Ranganatha Saraswati had found it in 1926.

s: What are the Nagarjunakonda monuments rebuilt on higher ground at Anupu and on the island known as?
x: The ASI rebuilt the submerged monuments at Anupu and on the island, called the 'Transplanted Monuments'.

x: The site was submerged after 1960; 1926 is the year of its discovery.

x: The island museum on the hilltop was opened by the ASI in 1966.

s: Where were Santamula's Ashvamedha altar and an amphitheatre found?
x: Nagarjunakonda finds include an amphitheatre, Santamula's Ashvamedha altar, a Sati sculpture and 30+ stupas.

s: Who discovered the Buddhist site of Salihundam?
x: Salihundam was discovered by Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy; A. Ranganatha Saraswati found Nagarjunakonda in 1926.

x: Bojjannakonda has a monolithic Buddha in Dhyana mudra and belongs to the Mahayana-Vajrayana phase.

s: What minimum lease period did the AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act, 1956 prescribe?

Ceiling per family unit (wet land) – 35-54 acres
Ceiling per family unit (dry land) – 10-27 acres

o: The land after six years of cultivation

s: On the report of which committee was the AP (Andhra Area) Tenancy Act, 1956 based?
x: The AP Andhra Area Tenancy Act, 1956 was based on the report of the Subba Rao Committee.

s: What was the maximum area retainable under the 1973 AP Land Reforms Act?
x: The maximum retainable area was 54 acres of ‘K’ grade, the lowest-grade, land.

Created the National Land Reforms Council
Permitted unrestricted transfer of tribal land to non-tribals
Abolished all tenancy in the Andhra area

s: Who was the Chief Minister when the Land Reforms Bill that led to the 1973 AP Ceiling Act was brought?

x: The 1961 Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings Act was AP's first, weak ceiling law; the 1973 Act followed.

s: On the report of which commission was the BC reservation in Andhra Pradesh raised to 44% in 1986?

x: The Six-Point Formula of 1973 was implemented through Article 371D, inserted by the 32nd Constitutional Amendment in 1973.

x: Backward Muslims got 4% reservation under BC-E, introduced in 2007.

s: Who piloted the Madras Devadasi (Prevention of Dedication) Act of December 1947?

s: Which of the following practices were also covered by the Andhra Pradesh Devadasis (Prohibition of Dedication) Act, 1988?

x: Total prohibition came in 1995, after the Dubagunta movement (1992) and the arrack ban (1993); it was lifted in 1997.

s: On which date did Andhra Pradesh adopt Panchayati Raj?
x: AP adopted Panchayati Raj on 1 November 1959, second after Rajasthan (2 October 1959).

x: Rajasthan adopted Panchayati Raj on 2 October 1959; AP followed on 1 November 1959.

s: By an Act of which year did Mandal Praja Parishads replace Panchayat Samitis in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The 1986 Act under NTR replaced Panchayat Samitis with Mandal Praja Parishads.

s: Under which Chief Minister was the arrack ban of 1993 imposed in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Kotla Vijaya Bhaskara Reddy banned arrack in 1993; NTR brought total prohibition in 1995.

s: The Dubagunta anti-arrack movement of 1992 began in which district?
x: Dubagunta, the village of the 1992 anti-arrack movement, is in Nellore.

s: In which year was total prohibition, introduced in 1995, lifted in Andhra Pradesh?
x: NTR's 1995 total prohibition was lifted by Chandrababu Naidu in 1997.

s: Who among the following campaigned against the Bhogam system in Andhra?
x: Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu campaigned against the Bhogam (devadasi) system.

s: Which of the following scheme – Chief Minister – year sets is correctly matched?

s: Where was the first residential school in Andhra Pradesh (1971) set up?
x: The first residential school was set up at Sarvail in Nalgonda district in 1971, under P.V. Narasimha Rao.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?

s: In which year did N.T. Rama Rao introduce the Rs 2 per kg rice scheme?

s: In which year was Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University established?

s: In which year was the Rajiv Aarogyasri health insurance scheme launched in Andhra Pradesh?

s: Under which Chief Minister was the Indiramma housing scheme launched in Andhra Pradesh?

s: In which year were Nagarjuna University and Kakatiya University established?

s: In which year was the NTR University of Health Sciences, the first health university in India, set up?

s: Under which Chief Minister was the Janmabhoomi programme launched in Andhra Pradesh in 1997?

s: In which district of Uttar Pradesh is Mangroth, the first Gramdan village, located?

Goa, Daman and Diu were liberated in 1961

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about border consolidation?
o: Dadra and Nagar Haveli became a UT by the 10th Amendment
NEFA became the State of Arunachal Pradesh in 1972
Goa, Daman and Diu became a UT by the 12th Amendment
Pondicherry became a UT by the 14th Amendment
x: NEFA became a Union Territory in 1972 and the State of Arunachal Pradesh only in 1987.

s: Dadra and Nagar Haveli was a possession of which colonial power before it was freed in 1954?
x: Dadra and Nagar Haveli was Portuguese, never French.

s: Who led the Naga National Council (NNC), which opposed the Centre on the Naga question?
x: A.Z. Phizo's Naga National Council opposed the Centre; the Centre responded by creating Nagaland State in 1963.

s: How many border villages are covered under the Vibrant Villages Programme-II?
x: Vibrant Villages Programme-II covers 1,954 border villages in 15 States and 2 UTs; it was launched at Nathanpur, Cachar.

s: In which year did Arunachal Pradesh (formerly NEFA) become a full-fledged State?
x: NEFA became the Union Territory of Arunachal Pradesh in 1972 and a State in 1987.

s: After which event did Jawaharlal Nehru set up the National Integration Council in 1961?
x: The National Integration Council was established by Nehru in 1961 after the National Integration Conference.

s: In which year was the AP Official Languages Act, which made Telugu the official language of the State, passed?
x: The AP Official Languages Act, 1966 made Telugu the State's official language.

s:
Consider the following statements about national integration and language:
1. The National Integration Council was set up in 1961 by Jawaharlal Nehru.
2. The AP Official Languages Act made Telugu the official language of the State.
3. The National Integration Council was set up by Lal Bahadur Shastri.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Nehru set up the NIC in 1961, and the 1966 Official Languages Act made Telugu official; Shastri did not set it up.

s: Which Act allowed English to continue along with Hindi for the official purposes of the Union after the 15-year period ended in 1965?
x: The Official Languages Act, 1963 let English continue with Hindi for Union purposes beyond 1965; it was amended in 1967.

s: Which committee of 1949 helped set the agenda for land reform in India?
x: The Kumarappa Committee of 1949 set the land reform agenda; Phase I of land reform covered 1947-70.

s: Which land reform brought about two crore tenants into direct contact with the State?
x: Abolition of intermediaries, regarded as the most successful reform, brought about two crore tenants into direct contact with the State.

s: In which State was Operation Barga (1977), the notable exception to failed tenancy reform, carried out?
x: Operation Barga (1977) was carried out in West Bengal, not Kerala.

s: Under the land-ceiling guidelines of 1972, what was the unit for applying the ceiling?
x: From 1972 the family, not the individual landholder, was made the unit for ceilings.

s: In which of the following regions did land consolidation succeed particularly?
o: Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
x: Land consolidation achieved notable success in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.

s: What did the Prakasam Committee, constituted in 1938, recommend?
o: Declaration of Telugu as a Classical Language
x: The Prakasam Committee of 1938 recommended the abolition of intermediaries.

s: The First Constitutional Amendment was significant for land reforms because it:
o: abolished all tenancy arrangements throughout India
shielded zamindari abolition measures from legal challenge
x: The First Amendment provided constitutional protection to zamindari abolition measures, helping shield them from legal challenge.

s: The failure of land reforms to overcome ceiling and tenancy problems contributed to the emergence of which of the following?
x: The failure of land reforms, particularly regarding ceilings and tenancy, contributed to the Naxalbari revolt of 1967.

s: What are transfers of land in others' names to defeat ceiling laws known as?
x: Benami transfers helped defeat the objectives of ceiling laws; oral leases and exemptions also weakened land reforms.

s: A major limitation of the abolition of zamindari and jagirdari was that it:
o: Changed the revenue hierarchy but left tenancy and landholding inequalities
x: Abolition mainly altered the revenue hierarchy; it did not by itself resolve tenancy problems and unequal landholding.

s: Raj Krishna classified land reforms into which four categories?
x: Raj Krishna classified land reforms as liberative, distributive, organisational and developmental.

s: When was the National Council for Land Reforms set up?
x: The National Council for Land Reforms was set up on 9 January 2008; 23 December 2004 is the Koneru Ranga Rao Committee.

s: Who chairs the National Council for Land Reforms?
x: The National Council for Land Reforms is chaired by the Prime Minister.

s: Tenancy reform capped rent at what share of the produce?
x: Tenancy laws capped rent at one-fourth to one-sixth of the produce.

s: Which State was the first to abolish zamindari, in 1950?
x: UP (1950) is the first State to abolish zamindari, though Madras's 1948 Act was passed earlier.

s: What did Jagir and Sarfekhas lands become after the abolition of intermediaries in Telangana?
x: Jagir and Sarfekhas lands became Diwani, or ryotwari, lands after the abolition measures.

s: In which year was the Hyderabad Jagirdari Abolition Regulation enacted?
x: The Hyderabad Jagirdari Abolition Regulation was enacted in 1949 to abolish intermediaries in Telangana.

s:
Consider the following statements about the abolition of intermediaries:
1. The 1967 extension of the Andhra Inams Act to Telangana was upheld by the High Court.
2. Zamindari estates in the Andhra area were abolished by the Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948.
3. The Abolition of Telangana Inams Act was passed in 1955.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The Madras Estates Act is of 1948 and the Telangana Inams Act of 1955; the 1967 extension of the Andhra Inams Act to Telangana was struck down by the High Court.

s: In which year was the Andhra Inams Act enacted?
x: The Andhra Inams Act is of 1956; 1955 is the Telangana Inams Act and 1948 the Madras Estates Act.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Telangana inams legislation?
o: The Telangana Inams Act was enacted in 1955.
The 1967 extension of the Andhra Inams Act to Telangana was upheld by the High Court.
Religious and charitable inams were exempted.
The Act was stalled in courts.
x: The 1967 extension of the Andhra Inams Act to Telangana was struck down, not upheld, by the High Court.

s: Which Act abolished the zamindari estates in the Andhra area in 1948?
o: Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act
AP Ceiling on Agricultural Holdings Act
x: In the Andhra area, zamindari estates were abolished by the Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948; the Jagirdari Regulation of 1949 was for Telangana.

s: Which approach to tribal policy was favoured by Jawaharlal Nehru over both isolation and forced assimilation?
o: Forced assimilation into the dominant society
x: Nehru rejected both the museum approach of isolation and forced assimilation, favouring integration while respecting tribal identity and institutions.

s: Which of the following is NOT a principle of the Tribal Panchsheel?
o: Tribes should develop along the lines of their own genius.
Tribal areas should be subjected to maximum administrative control.
Tribal languages should be encouraged and preserved.
Tribal communities should be trained to run their own administration.
x: The Tribal Panchsheel advocated avoiding over-administration, so 'maximum administrative control' is not one of its principles.

s: Verrier Elwin's work titled A Philosophy for NEFA primarily argued for which of the following?
o: Cultural autonomy and limits on land alienation
Complete assimilation and unrestricted land transfer
Expansion of commercial farming in tribal areas
x: A Philosophy for NEFA argued for cultural autonomy and limitations on the alienation of tribal land.

s: To whom is the formulation of the Tribal Panchsheel, under Nehru's influence, credited?
x: The Tribal Panchsheel is credited to Verrier Elwin, under the influence of Jawaharlal Nehru.

s: To which areas does the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 apply?
o: All urban areas in the North-East
Scheduled Areas covered by the Fifth Schedule
Only Union Territories with tribal populations
Autonomous districts under the Sixth Schedule only
x: PESA 1996 applies to Scheduled Areas in states covered by the Fifth Schedule; it does not apply to the Sixth Schedule autonomous district areas.

s: Where do the Chenchus of Andhra Pradesh mainly live?
x: The Chenchus live in the Nallamala of Kurnool, Prakasam and Guntur.

s: In which district is the Yanadi tribe chiefly found?
x: The Yanadi live mainly in Nellore, Chittoor and Prakasam.

s: Which of the following pairs (tribe – region) is correctly matched?
x: Savara, Jatapu and Gadaba live in Srikakulam-Vizianagaram; Koya are in the Godavari region and Chenchu in the Nallamala.

s: The Lambada (Sugali/Banjara) tribe is found in all of the following States EXCEPT:
x: The Lambada live in Telangana, AP, Karnataka and Maharashtra, not in Madhya Pradesh.

s: In which region of Andhra Pradesh do the Koya and Konda Reddi tribes mainly live?
x: The Koya and Konda Reddi live mainly in the Godavari region.

s: The Bagata, Kondadora and Poraja tribes mainly live in which agency area?
x: Bagata, Kondadora and Poraja live mainly in the Araku-Paderu agency of the north.

s: How many PVTGs did undivided Andhra Pradesh have?
x: Undivided AP had 12 PVTGs, second to Odisha's 13; India has 75.

s: Which State has more PVTGs than undivided Andhra Pradesh?
x: Odisha has 13 PVTGs, more than undivided AP's 12.

s: Which of the following is NOT a PVTG of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Koya is not in the PVTG list; Chenchu, Kolam and Thoti are among AP's 12 PVTGs.

s: How many Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) are there in India?
x: India has 75 PVTGs; undivided AP had 12, second only to Odisha (13).

s: With which of the following is Eetela Panduga, also known as Chaitrapurab, associated?
o: the harvest festival of the Lambadas
the birth ceremony of Koya boys
the spring festival of the Araku tribes
x: Eetela Panduga or Chaitrapurab is the spring festival of the Araku tribes, during which Dhimsa is danced.

s: What do the Lambadis call Deepavali?
x: The Lambadis call Deepavali Kalimas; Jari Gundu is another name for Heli Panduga.

s: Modakondamma, in whose honour an annual tribal jatara is held, is the goddess of which region?
x: Modakondamma is regarded as the goddess of the Paderu agency, where an annual tribal jatara is held.

s: Which tribe celebrates Bhumi Panduga, held before monsoon sowing and ending with the Kommu dance?
x: Bhumi Panduga is a Koya festival of the Godavari agency.

s: During Seethala Panduga, against which of the following do the Lambadis worship Seethala Mata as a guard?
x: Seethala Mata is believed to guard against smallpox.

s: By what other name is Heli Panduga, the Lambadi festival for newborn sons, known?
x: Heli Panduga is also called Jari Gundu and features the Jojer Nrutyam.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Dhimsa dance:
1. Its origin is traced to Koraput.
2. It is danced in circles with hands on one another's shoulders.
3. It is performed by groups of about 50-60 women.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Dhimsa originated in Koraput and is danced in circles with hands on the shoulders; the groups are of about 15-20 women, not 50-60.

s:
Consider the following pairs (dance – community):
1. Kommu – Koya
2. Gussadi – Lambada
3. Lambadi dance – Lambada/Sugali women
Which of the above pairs are correctly matched?
x: Kommu is the Koya dance and the Lambadi dance is by Lambada/Sugali women; Gussadi is a Gond dance.

s: The Dhimsa dance of the Andhra agency is chiefly performed by which of the following tribes?
o: Bagata, Gadaba, Kondadora, Poraja and Valmiki
x: Dhimsa is danced by the Bagata, Gadaba, Kondadora, Poraja and Valmiki (other sources add Savara, Jatapu, Khond and Kotia). The Gond perform Gussadi; Lambada/Sugali women perform the Lambadi dance; the Koya perform the Kommu (bison-horn) dance.

s: Where was the Guinness World Record for the largest Dhimsa dance (July 2026) set?
o: Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, Bhogapuram
x: Over 13,000 tribal women and girl students danced at the Bhogapuram airport in Vizianagaram; the certificate went to the AP Tribal Welfare Department.

s: What is the headgear of Kommu dancers of the Koya tribe made of?
x: Kommu is the Koya dance with bison-horn headgear.

s: Which tribe performs the Gussadi dance?
x: Gussadi is a dance of the Gond tribe (Telangana side), not of the Lambada.

s: The Savara language belongs to which language family?
x: Savara and Gadaba are Munda languages; Koya and Gondi are Dravidian.

s: Which tribal language of Andhra Pradesh has its own script?
x: Savara is the only AP tribal language with a script.

s: Which of the following is a Munda language?
x: Gadaba is Munda; Gondi, Kolami and Koya are Dravidian.

s: Who described a tribe as a 'segmental organisation' of equivalent multi-family groups?
x: Marshall Sahlins described a tribe as a segmental organisation of equivalent multi-family groups.

s: Who can amend the notified list of Scheduled Tribes under Article 342(2)?
x: Only Parliament can amend the list (Art. 342(2)); the President only notifies it after consulting the Governor.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's Scheduled Tribe profile (Census 2011)?
o: Odisha has the largest tribal population.
x: Madhya Pradesh, not Odisha, has the largest tribal population; the other three statements are correct.

s: Under which Article of the Constitution does the President notify the Scheduled Tribes after consulting the Governor?
x: Article 342 lets the President notify STs after consulting the Governor; only Parliament can change the list (Art. 342(2)).

s: Which of the following describes Chenchu social organisation?
x: The Chenchus are an endogamous tribe with exogamous clans (kulams/gothrams); they are patriarchal and patrilineal.

s: Regarding Chenchu village offices and clans, which pair is correctly matched?
x: Raju is associated with the Bhoomani clan; Mantri with Kumakula, and Kolagadu with the Dasari, Uttaluri or Mandla clans.

s: With which tribe is the Ghotul youth dormitory associated?
x: Ghotul is the example of a youth dormitory associated with the Muria of Chhattisgarh.

s: In Chenchu society, who officiate marriages along with the Raju and the Mantri?
x: Raju, Mantri and Kolagadu, from different clans, officiate marriages; Bhoomani and Kumakula are clans.

s: Idital wall paintings are associated with which tribal community?
x: Idital wall paintings are associated with the Savara, also known as Sora, community.

s: With which tribe is Pithora painting particularly associated?
o: Rathwa of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh
x: Pithora is associated with the Rathwa community of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh.

s: On which of the following does the agency economy of the Araku belt rest?
o: Podu, minor forest produce, coffee and horticulture
Tea plantations, jute mills and inland shipping
Marine fishing, salt production and shipbuilding
x: The agency economy combines podu (shifting cultivation) and minor forest produce with coffee and horticulture in the Araku belt.

s: In the agency areas, what does 'Podu' refer to?
x: Podu is the shifting cultivation of the agency areas.

s: Which tribal community of Andhra Pradesh is traditionally known for basket making?
x: The Yerukala are traditional basket makers, weaving baskets from bamboo and wild date palm spines.

s: Who led the Rampa Rebellion of 1922–24 in the Eastern Ghats?
x: Alluri Sitarama Raju led the Rampa Rebellion in the Eastern Ghats from 1922 to 1924.
